lesson.title: Explaining Why and How
lesson.subtitle: Reasons, descriptions and the self
lesson.description: Ask why something happened and describe different ways of doing things.

learning_objectives: Ask reasons with 为什么 (wèi shénme).
Distinguish 这么 (zhème) and 那么 (nàme) in a description.
Refer back to oneself with 自己 (zìjǐ).

metadata.audience: HSK 3.0 Level 2 learners with Level 1 foundations

overview.topic_description: Ask why something happened and describe different ways of doing things.
overview.focus: Ask reasons with 为什么 (wèi shénme).

items.meaning_en: so; like that; in that case

examples.pinyin: nǐ zěnme nàme gāoxìng?
examples.english: Why are you so happy?
examples.teaching_note: 那么 modifies degree here (so/that); the syllabus also labels it a demonstrative and a conjunction.

examples.hanzi: 天气那么冷，大家都在家。
examples.pinyin: tiānqì nàme lěng, dàjiā dōu zài jiā.
examples.english: The weather is so cold that everyone is at home.
examples.teaching_note: 那么 modifies degree here (so/that); the syllabus also labels it a demonstrative and a conjunction.

items.pos_note: 那么 modifies degree here (so/that); the syllabus also labels it a demonstrative and a conjunction.

examples.pinyin: wǒ bù xǐhuan nàyàng de yīfu.
examples.english: I don't like clothes like that.
examples.teaching_note: A short spoken example using 那样.

examples.pinyin: nàyàng de shūbāo hěn piányi.
examples.english: That kind of schoolbag is inexpensive.
examples.teaching_note: A simple written example using 那样.

examples.pinyin: nǐ wèi shénme bú qù?
examples.english: Why aren't you going?
examples.teaching_note: 为什么 is an interrogative meaning “why”.

examples.hanzi: 大家都知道他为什么每天学汉语。
examples.pinyin: dàjiā dōu zhīdào tā wèi shénme měi tiān xué Hànyǔ.
examples.english: Everyone knows why he studies Chinese every day.
examples.teaching_note: 为什么 is an interrogative meaning “why”.

items.pos_note: 为什么 is an interrogative meaning “why”.

items.meaning_en: so; this; to such a degree

examples.pinyin: zěnme zhème guì?
examples.english: Why is it so expensive?
examples.teaching_note: 这么 modifies degree here (so/this); its demonstrative use is retained in the POS tags.

examples.hanzi: 今天这么冷，大家都不出门。
examples.pinyin: jīntiān zhème lěng, dàjiā dōu bù chūmén.
examples.english: It's so cold today that no one is going out.
examples.teaching_note: 这么 modifies degree here (so/this); its demonstrative use is retained in the POS tags.

items.pos_note: 这么 modifies degree here (so/this); its demonstrative use is retained in the POS tags.

examples.pinyin: nǐ wèi shénme zhèyàng shuō?
examples.english: Why do you say it like that?
examples.teaching_note: A short spoken example using 这样.

examples.pinyin: lǎoshī zhèyàng jiāo xuéshēng xiě zì.
examples.english: The teacher teaches the students to write characters this way.
examples.teaching_note: A simple written example using 这样.

examples.pinyin: wǒ zìjǐ lái!
examples.english: I'll do it myself!
examples.teaching_note: A short spoken example using 自己.

examples.hanzi: 这个孩子能自己穿衣服。
examples.pinyin: zhège háizi néng zìjǐ chuān yīfu.
examples.english: This child can get dressed without help.
examples.teaching_note: A simple written example using 自己.

examples.pinyin: dàjiā dōu lái le.
examples.english: Everyone has come.
examples.teaching_note: 大家 refers to everyone present or in the relevant group; 都 reinforces “all.”

examples.pinyin: dàjiā xiàwǔ liǎng diǎn lái shàngkè.
examples.english: Everyone comes to class at two in the afternoon.
examples.teaching_note: A simple class schedule: 来上课 describes coming to attend a lesson.

examples.pinyin: zhège duōshao qián?
examples.english: How much does this cost?
examples.teaching_note: 多少钱 is the routine shopping question for a price.

examples.pinyin: zhège bān yǒu duōshao xuéshēng?
examples.english: How many students are in this class?
examples.teaching_note: School or study context showing 多少 in a simple description.

items.pos_note: Interrogative pronoun asking how many or how much (多少钱、多少人). It is not itself a classifier and can directly precede a noun.

examples.pinyin: nǐ xǐhuan nǎ běn shū?
examples.english: Which book do you like?
examples.teaching_note: 哪 selects one among known choices; 本 is the measure word for books.

examples.hanzi: 老师问：“你们想读哪本书？”
examples.pinyin: lǎoshī wèn: “nǐmen xiǎng dú nǎ běn shū?”
examples.english: The teacher asked, “Which book would you like to read?”
examples.teaching_note: The question word comes before the book classifier.

grammar_points.title: Asking for a reason
grammar_points.explanation: 为什么 (wèi shénme) asks for the reason; a natural reply often begins with 因为 (yīnwèi).

grammar_points.title: Referring to manner and self
grammar_points.explanation: 这样 (zhèyàng) or 那样 (nàyàng) indicates a way of doing something; 自己 (zìjǐ) identifies the person acting independently.

questions.prompt: What is happening in the second part of the reading?
questions.explanation: Use the details in the second paragraph to justify your answer.
questions.answer: Another student says, “Don’t write it that way; write it this way.” The teacher asks him to explain again.

questions.prompt: Write the Mandarin sentence for: Why are you not going to school today? Give both Hanzi and pinyin.
questions.explanation: Use the expressions and grammar you have practised. Suggested answer: 为什么你今天不去学校？ (Wèi shénme nǐ jīntiān bú qù xuéxiào?)
questions.answer: 为什么你今天不去学校？ (Wèi shénme nǐ jīntiān bú qù xuéxiào?)

patterns.title: Asking for a reason
patterns.explanation_en: 为什么 (wèi shénme) asks for the reason; a natural reply often begins with 因为 (yīnwèi).

examples.hanzi: 为什么你今天不去学校？
examples.pinyin: Wèi shénme nǐ jīntiān bú qù xuéxiào?
examples.english: Why are you not going to school today?

examples.hanzi: 因为我自己做完了这道题！
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi wǒ zìjǐ zuò wán le zhè dào tí!
examples.english: Because I finished this problem by myself!

patterns.pattern_hanzi: 为什么 + 分句？ / 主语 + 为什么 + 动词短语？
patterns.pattern_pinyin: wèishénme + fēnjù? / zhǔyǔ + wèishénme + dòngcí duǎnyǔ?
patterns.pattern_pseudo_translation: 为什么 + <clause>？ / <subject> + 为什么 + <verb phrase>？

patterns.title: Referring to manner and self
patterns.explanation_en: 这样 (zhèyàng) or 那样 (nàyàng) indicates a way of doing something; 自己 (zìjǐ) identifies the person acting independently.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zìjǐ shì yi shì.
examples.english: I want to try it myself.

examples.hanzi: 我先看书，再照着上面的方法做。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiān kàn shū, zài zhàozhe shàngmian de fāngfǎ zuò.

reading.title: Explaining Why and How — short reading

paragraphs.hanzi: 老师问学生为什么这样写，学生说自己以前学过这个词。
paragraphs.pinyin: Lǎoshī wèn xuéshēng wèi shénme zhèyàng xiě, xuéshēng shuō zìjǐ yǐqián xué guo zhè ge cí.
paragraphs.english: The teacher asks why the student wrote it that way, and the student says they learned the word before.

paragraphs.hanzi: 另一个学生说：“不要那么写，应该这么写。”老师请他再解释一下。
paragraphs.pinyin: Lìng yí ge xuéshēng shuō: “Bú yào nàme xiě, yīnggāi zhème xiě.” Lǎoshī qǐng tā zài jiěshì yíxià.
paragraphs.english: Another student says, “Don’t write it that way; write it this way.” The teacher asks him to explain again.

questions.prompt_en: What do we learn about the people or situation in the first part of the reading?
questions.answer_en: The teacher asks why the student wrote it that way, and the student says they learned the word before.

questions.prompt_en: What happens or is explained in the second part of the reading?
questions.answer_en: Another student says, “Don’t write it that way; write it this way.” The teacher asks him to explain again.

teaching_plan.common_pitfall: Do not translate 这么 (zhème) and 这样 (zhèyàng) as identical in every context: one often modifies degree, the other a way or manner.
teaching_plan.pronunciation_focus: Practise the fourth tone in 这 (zhè) and 那 (nà), and the third-tone pair in 自己 (zìjǐ).
